index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 CommandLine="*enc*"
| where match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\.exe$")
| where match(Image, "(?i)\\\\powershell\.exe$")
| where match(CommandLine, "(?i)[\s\"/-]-?enc(odedcommand)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}")
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\.exe$") AND match(Image, "(?i)\\\\powershell\.exe$") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s-e(nc|ncodedcommand)?\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\.exe$") AND match(Image, "(?i)\\\\powershell\.exe$") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s-(e|enc|ec|encodedcommand)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | where NOT match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s-(e|enc|ec|encodedcommand)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}.*(-File|Admin-Automation)") AND NOT match(ParentCommandLine, "(?i)/automation") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook|powerpnt|msaccess|mspub|onenote)\\.exe$") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)(^|\\s)[-/](encodedcommand|encodedcomman|encodedcomma|encodedcomm|encodedcom|encodedco|encodedc|encoded|encode|encod|enco|enc|en|ec|e)[\\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | eval cl=replace(CommandLine,"[\"'^`]","") | where (match(Image,"(?i)\\\\(powershell|pwsh)\\.exe$") OR match(cl,"(?i)(powershell|pwsh)") OR match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook|powerpnt|msaccess|mspub|onenote)\\.exe$")) AND match(cl,"(?i)(^|\\s)[-/–—](encodedcommand|encodedcomman|encodedcomma|encodedcomm|encodedcom|encodedco|encodedc|encoded|encode|encod|enco|enc|ec|en|e)[\\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{30,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | eval cl=replace(CommandLine,"[\"'^`]","") | where match(Image,"(?i)\\\\(powershell|pwsh)\\.exe$") AND (match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook|powerpnt|msaccess|mspub|onenote)\\.exe$") OR match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|conhost)\\.exe$")) AND match(cl,"(?i)(^|\\s)[-/](encodedcommand|encodedcomman|encodedcomma|encodedcomm|encodedcom|encodedco|encodedc|encoded|encode|encod|enco|enc)[\\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{30,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

gates.gate_spl: search index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 | eval cl=replace(CommandLine,"[\"'^`]","") | where match(Image,"(?i)\\\\(powershell|pwsh)\\.exe$") AND (match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook|powerpnt|msaccess|mspub|onenote)\\.exe$") OR match(ParentImage,"(?i)\\\\(cmd|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|conhost)\\.exe$")) AND match(cl,"(?i)(^|\\s)[-/](encodedcommand|encodedcomman|encodedcomma|encodedcomm|encodedcom|encodedco|encodedc|encoded|encode|encod|enco|enc)[\\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{30,}") | bin _time span=20m | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by _time Computer, User, ParentImage, Image | sort 0 - count

findings.detail: The first exclusion 'NOT match(CommandLine, ...-(e|enc|ec|encodedcommand)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}.*(-File|Admin-Automation))' lets an attacker suppress the entire alert by appending the literal token '-File' anywhere after the base64 blob. The attacker fully controls the powershell CommandLine, so adding a harmless/ignored '-File' string (or 'Admin-Automation') defeats detection while the malicious -enc payload still executes.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the '-File' / 'Admin-Automation' CommandLine exclusion entirely, or tie exclusion to a trusted signed-script path + known parent, not to a token the attacker controls.

findings.detail: The encoded-flag regex '-(e|enc|ec|encodedcommand)' only matches those exact tokens, but PowerShell accepts any unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand. Variants '-en', '-enco', '-encod', '-encode', '-encoded', '-encodedc', '-encodedcomman' all run the encoded payload and none are matched by the regex, so the detection is fully bypassed.
findings.fix_hint: Match the prefix family, e.g. (?i)\s[-/](e|en|enc|ec|enco|encod|encode|encoded|encodedc|encodedco|encodedcom|encodedcomm|encodedcomma|encodedcomman|encodedcommand)\b or simply (?i)\s-e[ncodfary]*\s and anchor on the base64 blob.

findings.detail: The flag/value separator is hard-coded to whitespace ('\s+'). PowerShell also accepts the colon form '-enc:JAB...' and the slash prefix '/enc'. 'powershell -enc:<base64>' satisfies no whitespace between flag and value so it evades the CommandLine regex.
findings.fix_hint: Allow colon or whitespace separators and both -/ prefixes: (?i)[\s][-/]enc(odedcommand)?[\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}.

findings.detail: Image is anchored to '\\powershell\.exe$'. A renamed/copied PowerShell binary (e.g. copy powershell.exe to C:\Users\Public\svc.exe) or PowerShell Core 'pwsh.exe' spawned from Office is not matched, even though OriginalFileName/parent still reveal the activity.
findings.fix_hint: Also key on OriginalFileName='PowerShell.EXE'/'pwsh.dll' and Description, or detect any child of Office that carries -enc regardless of Image name.

findings.detail: ParentImage only covers winword|excel|outlook. Common Office macro hosts powerpnt.exe (PowerPoint), msaccess.exe, mspub.exe, onenote.exe and the Office COM broker are excluded, so a malicious PowerPoint/Access macro spawning powershell -enc is missed.

The ParentCommandLine '/automation' exclusion drops any event where the Office parent was launched with '/automation'. Office started via COM automation legitimately carries '/automation', and an attacker invoking Office through COM (a documented maldoc-adjacent technique) can inherit this switch to self-exclude.
findings.fix_hint: Do not blanket-exclude on /automation; restrict to a known automation service account/host, or remove it and rely on child -enc as the signal.

findings.detail: Detection relies on ParentCommandLine being populated for the exclusion logic; when Sysmon config does not capture ParentCommandLine (field absent), match() returns false and the exclusion is inert - behaviour differs silently across hosts, making results inconsistent.
findings.fix_hint: Explicitly handle null (e.g. coalesce ParentCommandLine to "") and document the required Sysmon config schema version.

findings.detail: The exclusion regex uses an unbounded '.*' between the base64 class and the '(-File|Admin-Automation)' alternation over the full CommandLine; combined with three sequential match()/where stages this is backtracking-prone on long encoded command lines.
findings.fix_hint: Replace '.*' with a bounded/non-greedy class and pre-filter with indexed terms (TERM(-enc)) before regex where().

evasion_events.note: Appending the literal '-File' after the base64 satisfies the first NOT-match exclusion and suppresses the alert even though -enc payload runs. Search currently misses it; it must match.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -WindowStyle hidden -enco JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdABXAGUAYgBDAGwAaQBlAG4AdAA7AA==</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n invoice.docm</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Uses abbreviated flag '-enco' (valid PowerShell prefix of -EncodedCommand) which the regex alternation (e|enc|ec|encodedcommand) does not match. Fully evaded.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS04.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc:JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdABXAGUAYgBDAGwAaQBlAG4AdAA7AA==</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\bwayne</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\OUTLOOK.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\OUTLOOK.EXE"</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Colon separator '-enc:<base64>' defeats the '\s+' whitespace requirement in the CommandLine regex. Must match.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS04.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Users\Public\svc.exe</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>svc.exe -enc JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdABXAGUAYgBDAGwAaQBlAG4AdAA7AA==</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\bwayne</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE" /e budget.xlsm</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Renamed PowerShell binary (copied to svc.exe); OriginalFileName still PowerShell.EXE. Image regex '\\powershell\.exe$' fails so detection is missed.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdABXAGUAYgBDAGwAaQBlAG4AdAA7AA==</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\POWERPNT.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\POWERPNT.EXE" /s deck.pptm</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: PowerPoint (POWERPNT.EXE) macro spawning powershell -enc. Parent alternation omits powerpnt so the event is not matched.

findings.detail: Detection fires only when ParentImage is an Office binary and the direct child carries -enc. Maldocs very commonly use an intermediate launcher: Office -> cmd.exe (or wscript/mshta/rundll32/conhost) -> powershell.exe -enc. In that chain the powershell EventCode=1 record has ParentImage=cmd.exe, which fails the ParentImage match, so the entire detection is bypassed while the encoded payload still runs. This is a mainstream TTP, not an edge case.
findings.fix_hint: Do not rely solely on the immediate ParentImage. Correlate across a process tree (e.g. join Office parent EventCode=1 to descendant powershell within a short window), or add a second rule that fires on any powershell -enc whose grandparent/ancestor is an Office process, or alert on encoded-command regardless of parent and risk-score by Office ancestry.

findings.detail: The CommandLine regex anchors the flag with (^|\s)[-/], requiring whitespace or line-start immediately before the dash. PowerShell accepts the parameter token in quotes, e.g. powershell "-enc" JAB... . Sysmon records the literal quotes, so the character before the dash is '"', which is not matched by (^|\s). The quoted-flag form executes the encoded payload but evades the regex even though ParentImage is Office.
findings.fix_hint: Relax the pre-flag anchor to also permit a quote/boundary, e.g. (^|[\s"'])[-/–—], and strip/normalise quotes out of CommandLine before matching so token obfuscation like "-enc", -e"nc" or -e^nc collapses to a canonical form.

findings.detail: The flag alternation includes the single/short tokens e, en, ec together with a separator [\s:]+ and a 20+ run of [A-Za-z0-9+/=]. Any Office-spawned process invoked as '-e <20+ alphanumeric token>' (or '/e ...') matches even when it is not an encoded PowerShell command. The 20-char base64 class also matches ordinary long alphanumeric arguments, so a non-PowerShell child could occasionally trip the rule.
findings.fix_hint: Constrain to real PowerShell/pwsh invocations (check Image OriginalFileName) and require the value to look like base64 (length multiple-of-4 or minimum ~40 chars) to reduce incidental matches on short flags like -e.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdAAgAEkATwAuAE0AZQBtAG8AcgB5AFMAdAByAGUAYQBtAA==</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>cmd.exe /c powershell -enc JABzAD0A...</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Intermediate-parent chain Office->cmd.exe->powershell. ParentImage=cmd.exe fails the Office ParentImage match, so the search misses it even though the -enc payload executes. Original benign sample had ParentImage=services.exe / svchost child.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" "-enc" JABzAD0ATgBlAHcALQBPAGIAagBlAGMAdAAgAEkATwAuAE0AZQBtAG8AcgB5AFMAdAByAGUAYQBtAA==</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Office->powershell direct, but the -enc flag is quoted ("-enc"). The char before the dash is a double-quote, so (^|\s)[-/] fails to match and the rule misses it despite valid Office parent and executing base64 payload.

findings.detail: The CommandLine flag alternation bottoms out at the 3-char token 'enc' (encodedcommand|...|enco|enc). PowerShell accepts any unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand, and powershell.exe specifically honors '-e' and '-ec' as EncodedCommand. 'powershell.exe -e <base64>' and 'powershell.exe -ec <base64>' are extremely common in maldoc/LOLBin chains and are fully missed because neither '-e' nor '-ec' is in the alternation. Note this is NOT the old prior-finding false-positive issue (tokens e/en/ec were removed from the regex) - removing them created a detection gap for the shortest legal abbreviations.
findings.fix_hint: Extend the alternation to include the ec and e abbreviations, e.g. match on [-/](e|ec|enc|enco|...|encodedcommand) while keeping the 30+ base64 class and [\s:]+ separator to control false positives.

findings.detail: Image is matched with a hard literal regex \\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$. A copied/renamed PowerShell binary (e.g. C:\Users\Public\upd.exe, svhost.exe, pwsh_update.exe) run from an Office/LOLBin parent with -enc still executes but has an Image that does not end in powershell.exe/pwsh.exe, so the whole rule is bypassed. Sysmon EventCode=1 carries OriginalFileName=PowerShell.EXE even when the file is renamed, but the search never references it.
findings.fix_hint: OR in a check on OriginalFileName (or Product/Description) matching PowerShell, e.g. match(OriginalFileName,"(?i)^powershell") so renamed binaries are still caught.

findings.detail: The ParentImage allow-list is a fixed set (winword/excel/outlook/powerpnt/msaccess/mspub/onenote and cmd/wscript/cscript/mshta/rundll32/regsvr32/conhost). Office-origin encoded-PowerShell can be spawned via a parent not in the list - WmiPrvSE.exe (DDE/WMI), explorer.exe (shell), taskeng.exe/svchost.exe (scheduled task), or LOLBins like forfiles.exe, pcalua.exe, wmic.exe, msbuild.exe. Any of these as the immediate parent of powershell -enc evades the rule even though the TTP matches.
findings.fix_hint: Either broaden the parent list (wmiprvse, explorer, forfiles, pcalua, wmic, msbuild, taskeng) or decouple: alert on powershell -enc regardless of parent and risk-score on suspicious ancestry rather than requiring a fixed direct parent.

findings.detail: The base64 argument class requires {30,} characters of [A-Za-z0-9+/=]. Short encoded commands (a one-line downloader can be <30 chars of base64 after UTF-16LE encoding of a very short script, or split across variables) fall below the threshold and are missed. The threshold trades recall for FP control and is a single point of brittleness.
findings.fix_hint: Lower the minimum to ~12-16 base64 chars, or gate purely on the presence of the enc flag + a base64-looking token and move length filtering into risk scoring.

evasion_events.note: Office parent, real powershell.exe, but uses the 2-char '-e' abbreviation of -EncodedCommand. Current regex min token is 'enc', so this fully evades even though it executes the base64 payload.

evasion_events.note: powershell.exe copied/renamed to upd.exe and launched from WINWORD with -EncodedCommand. Image fails the \\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$ match; OriginalFileName still says PowerShell.EXE but the search never checks it, so the rule is bypassed.

Maldoc uses WMI (Win32_Process.Create) so the encoded powershell's immediate parent is WmiPrvSE.exe, which is not in the ParentImage allow-list. Payload runs but the parent check fails and the rule misses it.
